The compliment and taxi are preserved because neither is logically incompatible with wet hair or the missing umbrella.

story: A painter creates a detailed painting of a tiger using ordinary oil paint in a normal brushed layer. He is especially proud of the tiger’s eyes and hopes the painting will lead to further commissions from a local gallery. After finishing the piece, he leaves it indoors at room temperature while he prepares the frame and exhibition paperwork. Twenty-four hours later, a gallery assistant arrives to help prepare the painting for display. While admiring a detail in one of the tiger’s eyes, she lightly touches the painted surface with a fingertip and accidentally smudges the still-wet paint.
query: Change this story to make the painter use ordinary acrylic paint instead, keeping all other background factors in the story the same.
expectation: The paint changes from ordinary oil to ordinary acrylic; after the unchanged 24-hour interval the acrylic is touch-dry, so the same light fingertip contact does not produce a wet-paint smudge.
knowledge_reasoning: Under ordinary room-temperature conditions and a normal brushed layer, acrylic paint generally becomes touch-dry well within 24 hours, whereas traditional oil paint commonly takes multiple days. Paint type therefore changes the surface state at the fixed time of contact. Because the touch is light rather than an abrasive cleaning action, the intended downstream distinction is specifically wet-paint smudging.
